svg.text: How the Raspberry Pi 4's USB, WiFi and Ethernet reach AmigaOS: the Alice68 kernel builds two Zorro II cards that Kickstart finds like real ones.
what is really there, driven by the Alice68 kernel
shared memory the kernel and the drivers both use
Pi 400 and CM4 alike (CM4: other WiFi chip)
the kernel reads Amiga buffers in place
virtual Zorro II bus - Kickstart autoconfigures it at every boot
magic, interrupt flag, what is plugged in
frames go to the stack in place
A USB host-controller driver: Neptune sees an 8-port
USB 2.0 root hub with every device the kernel offers.
Class drivers: USB drives and sticks (DOS volumes),
netdev interface: the stack and the driver call each
other directly; received frames are handed up in place.
Browsers, FTP, AmiSSL, ... - everything on the network.
Hardfiles and SD-card folders. At boot it reads the
WIFI folder and hands the firmware to the network card.
Both cards raise it when they have news: a finished
request, a new frame, a device plugged in. The drivers'
interrupt code takes it from there.
Keyboards and mice never go through a card:
the kernel keeps them on CPU1 and feeds them straight into the Amiga's own keyboard and mouse ports (virtual CIA) - from power-on, in Kickstart and WHDLoad, with no USB stack in AmigaOS.
HOW ONE REQUEST TRAVELS (a USB read, or a network frame being sent)
The Amiga driver writes the request
into a free slot on the card: what to do,
how much, where the 68k buffer is.
The kernel on CPU1 does it
on the real hardware (xHCI, WiFi chip,
GENET), reading the Amiga buffer in place.
level 2 (PORTS), as a real Zorro card
does when it has finished something.
it finds the finished slots and
replies to Neptune or the TCP/IP stack.
hardware, and nothing in AmigaOS polls it.
No real card has these IDs (0x6d73 is Emu68's manufacturer number); only
the drivers in ALICE68: know them. They do nothing on a PiStorm or in an emulator.
Workbench's ShowConfig lists both cards with Emu68's ROM board.
the cards keep the kernel's and the drivers' log rings, so
Alice68-USBLog, Alice68-WiFi LOG and Alice68-Monitor DUMP still read them after a hang.
no USB card; the network card's kernel side has CPU1 to itself.
the USB card stays empty - the kernel leaves the USB-A ports to
rondoval's xhci.device. Never run xhci.device while the kernel owns them.
the kernel leaves the Ethernet port alone, for rondoval's genet.device.
double-click Install in ALICE68: - it puts both drivers and the tools in place.
